From: Ava Chen <ava.chen@redwood.ai>

Subject: Commercial route & next steps — QuantumWave trial readiness

Thanks again for taking the time today, Jordan — great conversation. Quick recap from our side and a handful of concrete next steps so procurement and your engineering team can line things up: 

Key call takeaways:
- QuantumWave wants a short proof-of-value (PoV) to validate latency and cost at typical traffic patterns (approx. 8-12k tokens/day across two apps).
- Procurement indicated a preference for a PO (purchase order) rather than card payments; they also asked whether marketplace invoicing would be possible.
- Engineering will want a simple onboarding checklist and confirmation on whether dedicated capacity or a hosted sandbox is required for representative load.

Procurement / billing options we discussed (please confirm preferred route):
1) PO + invoice: Redwood issues invoice against a signed SOW/PO; billing begins on the effective date in the PO.
2) Card: immediate start (self-serve) — faster but procurement dislikes this.
3) Marketplace (AWS/GCP): can simplify invoicing and entitlements; requires vendor onboarding on your side.

Trial gating and success criteria we propose:
- Trial length: 7 calendar days from environment availability.
- Success metrics (attached CSV): 1) sustained 95th latency under 300ms for 95% of requests; 2) total token volume >= 60k across evaluation period; 3) integration of KV cache and prefix caching in staging.
- Billing start: we recommend billing begin on the first calendar day after procurement signs the PO (or immediately if you choose card/marketplace). If you'd like to delay billing until after success criteria are met, we can discuss crediting/backdating on a case-by-case basis.

Requested items for procurement to send back to us to keep things moving:
- High-level PO that references Redwood Quote QW-2026-013 or the SOW (attached).
- Procurement contact for invoicing (name + email).
- Any specific tax or remittance details.

Next steps (proposed):
- Jordan: Confirm preferred billing route (PO vs card vs marketplace) and copy procurement@quantumwave.ai on your reply.
- Procurement: If PO, send a draft PO referencing the SOW so we can validate terms and prepare DocuSign.
- Rishi / Dev: I’m looping you both in to confirm capacity recommendations and an integration checklist we can send to QuantumWave.

Attachments: SOW-trial-outline.pdf (stub), trial-success-metrics.csv (stub)

Thanks — I’ll wait for the confirmation and then circulate the DocuSign + HubSpot link.

—

Thanks Ava — helpful summary. A couple clarifications from our side: 

1) Procurement preference: PO. Our procurement lead (cc'd) will need an invoice and a SOW to attach. They'll also want standard terms (payment net-30).
2) Trial/billing timing: from the business side we prefer that billing starts only after we confirm the PoV success metrics are met (so we can avoid early spend). If that's a hard policy for Redwood, we can propose a compromise: billing starts once PO is executed, but if success criteria aren't met within 14 days we request a one-time credit. Is that feasible?
3) Marketplace: we'd like the marketplace route if possible — reduces internal vendor onboarding. Which marketplaces does Redwood support for invoicing?

From engineering: we want to make sure the trial environment matches our production-like load. Can your SE confirm whether a hosted sandbox can emulate our expected throughput or whether we need a dedicated pool?

Procurement — please take a look at the attached SOW and suggest next steps for the PO.

Hi all — quick technical run and recommendation. Thanks for the clear asks, Ava.

Short answers:
- Hosted sandbox: Yes — our hosted environment can emulate the requested throughput (8-12k tokens/day) with 95th latency targets in most cases. For initial validation we usually run on the hosted plan with autoscaling turned off to preserve deterministic latency.
- Dedicated pool: Not necessary for the PoV unless you plan to drive sustained concurrency > 40 RPS or use very long context windows (>8k tokens). If you do need dedicated capacity, a single T4-equivalent instance with 32GB would be sufficient for the expected traffic for a 7–14 day PoV.
- KV / prefix caching: Works fine in hosted; we recommend enabling prefix caching (config flag in the integration checklist) to improve cold-start behavior. There are no special infra changes needed.

Commercial/billing recommendation:
- Start the PoV immediately on hosted sandbox (no upfront charge) while procurement processes the PO.
- Procurement sends PO referencing Quote QW-2026-013 to sales@redwood.ai. We will prepare DocuSign with the SOW.
- Billing start: Redwood's standard is to start billing on the effective date in the PO. If QuantumWave prefers billing only after success criteria are met, we can accept a 14-day grace credit: if criteria are not met within 14 days we will issue a one-time credit equal to the billed amount for the PoV period (requires approval from commercial manager).

Next steps for Jordan / Procurement:
- Send PO (draft okay) to sales@redwood.ai referencing QW-2026-013.
- Provide invoicing contact details and remittance instructions.
- Confirm whether you want marketplace invoicing — we currently support AWS Marketplace and GCP Marketplace; enablement typically takes 5–10 business days for vendor onboarding.

I'll also share a short-run config snippet for the hosted sandbox and a pre-filled DocuSign template to speed the PO path.

—
